events.title: Birth at Purandar
events.summary: Sambhaji is born at Purandar fort to Shivaji and his first wife Saibai — Shivaji's eldest son.

events.title: Mother Saibai dies
events.summary: Saibai dies at Rajgad when Sambhaji is two. He is brought up largely by his grandmother Jijabai.

events.title: Married to Yesubai
events.summary: As a boy Sambhaji is married to Yesubai, daughter of Pilaji Shirke of the Konkan — a political match (the exact year is uncertain). Yesubai later runs the state's affairs from Raigad while Sambhaji campaigns.

events.title: Made a Mughal mansabdar at eight
events.summary: Under the Treaty of Purandar, Shivaji avoids personal Mughal service; instead the eight-year-old Sambhaji is enrolled as a Mughal mansabdar of 5,000.

events.title: With his father at Agra
events.summary: Sambhaji, aged nine, accompanies Shivaji to Aurangzeb's court and shares his house arrest.

events.title: Escape — hidden at Mathura
events.summary: After the escape from Agra, Sambhaji is left in hiding with trusted families at Mathura while Shivaji travels on in disguise; reports of his death are spread to throw off pursuers. He is brought back to the Deccan months later.

events.title: Scholar and poet: Budhbhushanam
events.summary: Sambhaji is educated in Sanskrit and Braj. He is credited with the Sanskrit work Budhbhushanam on statecraft — traditionally said to have been written at about 14 — and with Braj works such as Nayikabhed, Saatsatak and Nakhshikh.

events.title: Shivaji's coronation — Sambhaji is Yuvraj
events.summary: At Shivaji's coronation at Raigad, Sambhaji is recognised as heir apparent (Yuvraj). Court tensions with senior ministers and with his stepmother Soyarabai, mother of Rajaram, grow over the following years.

events.title: Defects to Diler Khan
events.summary: After clashes at court and confinement at Sringarpur, Sambhaji and Yesubai cross over to the Mughal general Diler Khan — a defection historians still debate.

events.title: Fall of Bhupalgad
events.summary: Diler Khan, with Sambhaji in his camp, takes the Maratha fort of Bhupalgad and mutilates the captured garrison. The brutality, and a Mughal order to send him to Delhi, reportedly turn Sambhaji against the Mughals.

events.title: Returns to Panhala
events.summary: Sambhaji escapes Diler Khan's camp near Bijapur and returns to Maratha territory. Shivaji keeps him at Panhala.

events.title: Rajaram placed on the throne
events.summary: Soyarabai and a group of senior ministers including Annaji Datto install the ten-year-old Rajaram at Raigad and try to keep Sambhaji out.

events.title: Shivaji dies at Raigad
events.summary: Shivaji dies at Raigad while Sambhaji is at Panhala. The succession is left unsettled.

events.title: Sambhaji takes control of Raigad
events.summary: Backed by commander-in-chief Hambirrao Mohite — Soyarabai's own brother — Sambhaji marches on Raigad and takes power. Rajaram is kept under watch.

events.title: Raid on Burhanpur
events.summary: Maratha cavalry strike deep into Mughal territory and plunder Burhanpur, a rich trading city — an early sign of the long war to come.

events.title: Crowned Chhatrapati
events.summary: Sambhaji is formally crowned the second Chhatrapati at Raigad. Kavi Kalash, a scholar from north India, becomes his closest adviser.

events.title: Prince Akbar takes refuge with Sambhaji
events.summary: Aurangzeb's son Akbar, whose rebellion in Rajasthan has failed, arrives in the Konkan seeking Maratha support for a bid for the Mughal throne. The alliance alarms Aurangzeb.

events.title: Court conspiracy crushed
events.summary: A plot against Sambhaji — involving Annaji Datto and other officials, and reportedly an approach to Prince Akbar — is uncovered; the leaders are executed. Soyarabai also dies in 1681; accounts of how differ.

events.title: Siege of Janjira
events.summary: Sambhaji tries to take the Siddis' island fortress of Janjira, even attempting to build a causeway to it, but has to abandon the siege when Mughal armies threaten.

events.title: Aurangzeb comes to the Deccan
events.summary: Aurangzeb arrives at Aurangabad with the imperial court and army to crush the Marathas and the Deccan sultanates. He never returns north; the Mughal–Maratha war lasts until his death in 1707.

events.title: Siege of Ramsej
events.summary: Aurangzeb opens his Deccan campaign by attacking Ramsej, a small fort near Nashik. Maratha tradition celebrates it holding out against successive Mughal commanders for about five years; Mughal-side accounts say Kasim Khan Kirmani took it after the garrison withdrew. Either way it became a byword for Maratha resistance.

events.title: Shahu born
events.summary: Yesubai gives birth to Shahu, later the fifth Chhatrapati, who will spend his childhood as a Mughal captive.

events.title: War with the Portuguese
events.summary: After the Portuguese besiege Ponda, Sambhaji relieves it and invades Goa's territory. He withdraws when a large Mughal army under Prince Muazzam enters the Konkan.

events.title: Bijapur falls to Aurangzeb
events.summary: After a long siege, Sikandar Adil Shah surrenders and the Bijapur Sultanate is annexed.

events.title: Prince Akbar leaves for Persia
events.summary: With no prospect of the Mughal throne, Akbar sails from the Konkan to Safavid Persia, where he dies in exile.

events.title: Golconda falls
events.summary: Golconda is taken after an eight-month siege; Abul Hasan Qutb Shah is imprisoned. With both Deccan sultanates gone, the Marathas face the full Mughal army alone.

events.title: Battle of Wai — Hambirrao Mohite killed
events.summary: The Marathas defeat a Mughal force near Wai, but commander-in-chief Hambirrao Mohite is killed — a heavy loss for Sambhaji.

events.title: Brought before Aurangzeb at Bahadurgad
events.summary: Sambhaji and Kavi Kalash are paraded at the Mughal camp at Bahadurgad. Sambhaji refuses to hand over his forts and treasure or to convert.

events.title: Rajaram takes charge at Raigad
events.summary: With Sambhaji captive, Yesubai and the ministers make Rajaram head of the state rather than the child Shahu, and plan to carry on the war.

events.title: Captured at Sangameshwar
events.summary: Mughal commander Muqarrab Khan surprises Sambhaji and Kavi Kalash with a small escort at Sangameshwar in the Konkan. Many accounts attribute the raid to information from Maratha rivals, including members of the Shirke family.

events.title: Executed at Tulapur
events.summary: After weeks of torture, Sambhaji and Kavi Kalash are put to death at Tulapur on the Bhima. His samadhi is at nearby Vadhu Budruk. Remembered in Maharashtra as Dharmaveer, his death hardened Maratha resistance rather than ending it.

events.title: Raigad falls; Yesubai and Shahu captured
events.summary: Rajaram has already slipped away south toward Gingee. When the Mughals take Raigad, Yesubai and seven-year-old Shahu are taken captive — they will be held for 18 years.

events.title: The war goes on: Santaji and Dhanaji
events.summary: Mobile Maratha armies led by Santaji Ghorpade and Dhanaji Jadhav fight across the Deccan, while Rajaram holds out at Gingee.

events.title: Rajaram dies at Sinhagad
events.summary: Rajaram dies at Sinhagad; his widow Tarabai leads the resistance in the name of their young son.
